messages.subject: robust Bayesian modeling
parts:
I know there has been some effort made to incorporate student t distributions into INLA, and that it has been challenging. 

 

I read with great interest this paper by Wang and Blei, http://www.cs.columbia.edu/~blei/papers/WangBlei2018.pdf, which contends that the better way to accomplish robust estimation is to set up exponential models with an additional localization parameter, and then set up a second likelihood to describe the probability of each observation, with its hyperparameter estimated by empirical bayes (or presumably some equivalent).  For a normal distribution, for example, the location parameter would get its own prior operating over each observation, which transforms the error distribution into the Student T.  The benefit is that the framework, once established, works for all types of exponential models (linear, logistic, poisson, etc.), with the difference on the front end being the “flag” of enabling robust estimation when it is desired, and under the hood, the parameterization of the second likelihood for the family in question to incorporate the localization option.  Worst case, the results come out the same, and best case, the results appear to be more robust.

 

Is this an approach that could be accommodated in INLA without violating any of its core assumptions, given INLA’s ability to handle multiple likelihoods? At least at a high level, this method sounds like the approach already taken to estimate measurement error, which seems to have been integrated successfully into the system.

 

As an alternative to the more ambitious idea above, at least for binary data, would it be possible for INLA to incorporate a robit option?  The probit and logit arguably are already special cases of the robit, and the robit would allow the degrees of freedom for the student T CDF to better accommodate outlier observations.

 

Some discussions of what this might look like, both generally and in Stan:

 

https://www.stat.purdue.edu/~chuanhai/teaching/Stat598A/robit.pdf

https://stackoverflow.com/questions/26447512/how-to-run-a-robit-model-in-stan

 

Jonathan
